*Hetuvārādiniddesa* (Ya 1.2.2) is a section of the *Yamaka*, the sixth text of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka in the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Functioning as an analytical exposition (*niddesa*) following the *Mūlavāraniddesa* in the opening division of the work, it provides the detailed catechism for root-conditions and related terms [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral lists one translation in a single language, but records no external or cross-canonical parallels [SuttaCentral].

While no cross-language parallels meeting the threshold are identified by DharmaNexus, the text displays extensive internal text-reuse across the Pali Abhidhamma corpus, sharing 63 matching passages with five other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest shared passages occur in connection with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (19 matches, with its longest shared segment running from §3.1_2–6.1 to §290_1–293) and the preceding *Mūlavāraniddesa* (Ya 1.2.1; 19 matches, longest segment §1.1–2.1_0 to §45.1–46.1) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits direct structural and phrastic reuse with the corresponding matrix summaries *Hetuvārādiuddesa* (Ya 1.1.2; 3 matches) and *Mūlavārauddesa* (Ya 1.1.1; 14 matches), as well as further Abhidhamma expositions including *Paṇṇattivāraniddesa* (Ya 9.1.2; 8 matches) [DharmaNexus].
